works.title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools (2nd ed.)
works.authors: Alfred V. Aho, Monica S. Lam, Ravi Sethi, Jeffrey D. Ullman
works.note: The canonical compiler text: names and teaches lexing, regex-to-automata, recursive-descent and LR parsing, ASTs, symbol tables, panic-mode recovery (Aho's own books page, loaded live, dates the AW printing 2007).

works.title: Crafting Interpreters
works.venue: Genever Benning; full text at craftinginterpreters.com
works.note: Modern implementation-first treatment: scanning, recursive descent with panic-mode synchronization, a tree-walk interpreter with REPL prompt, and Pratt parsing in the bytecode compiler (TOC loaded live).

works.title: On the Translation of Languages from Left to Right
works.note: The paper that defined LR(k) parsing; canon naming source behind the Dragon Book's ch. 4 treatment (publisher page not loadable this session).

works.title: Top Down Operator Precedence
works.note: Naming paper for Pratt (top-down operator-precedence) parsing; ACM DL and author pages not loadable this session.

works.title: "Maximal-Munch" Tokenization in Linear Time
works.note: Canonical paper on the maximal-munch (longest-match) tokenization rule and its linear-time realization (citation confirmed live on Reps's Wisconsin page).

works.title: Packrat Parsing: Simple, Powerful, Lazy, Linear Time
works.note: Naming paper for packrat (memoizing PEG) parsing; confirmed live on Ford's own packrat/PEG bibliography page.

works.title: Scannerless Generalized-LR Parsing
works.venue: Technical Report P9707, Programming Research Group, University of Amsterdam
works.note: The SGLR report that made scannerless parsing practical (lexical + context-free syntax in one grammar); confirmed live via Visser's researchr bibliography and eelcovisser.org.

works.title: Monadic Parser Combinators
works.venue: Technical Report NOTTCS-TR-96-4, University of Nottingham
works.note: The tutorial that established monadic parser combinators as the FP idiom for building parsers (citation confirmed live on Hutton's Nottingham publications page).

works.title: Programming Techniques: Regular Expression Search Algorithm
works.note: Canon naming/implementation paper for regular-expression matching (Thompson NFA construction); ACM DL not loadable this session; Dragon Book ch. 3 is the modern teaching treatment.

works.title: Prettyprinting
works.note: The canonical linear-time pretty-printing algorithm paper that most later pretty-printer libraries descend from; ACM DL page not loadable this session.

works.title: Algol 60 Translation: An Algol 60 Translator for the X1 and Making a Translator for Algol 60
works.note: Primary source of the shunting-yard algorithm for infix-expression translation (record loaded live in the CWI institutional repository).

works.title: Domain-Specific Languages
works.note: The DSL pattern catalog: names Semantic Model and teaches Symbol Table and Parser Combinator as reusable DSL-implementation patterns (book page + ISBN loaded live on martinfowler.com).

works.title: Enforcing Strict Model-View Separation in Template Engines
works.note: The StringTemplate paper - the principled treatment of template-engine design and model-view separation; author-site PDF retrieved but no citation page loadable this session.

works.title: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture
works.note: Names Template View (the template-engine pattern for web pages) and Serialized LOB in its catalog (book page + ISBN loaded live on martinfowler.com).

works.title: Protocol Buffers Encoding (programming guide)
works.note: The living authoritative definition of base-128 varints, ZigZag encoding, LEN length-prefixed records, and field-tag wire format (page loaded live; confirms all four mechanisms).

works.title: DWARF Debugging Information Format, Version 5
works.note: Already in corpus (emb passes); pass-8 lens: normatively defines LEB128, the other canonical variable-length integer encoding beside protobuf varints.

works.title: ITU-T X.690 - ASN.1 Encoding Rules: BER, CER and DER
works.note: The standards-grade definition of type-length-value encoding (BER) and of canonical/distinguished encodings (CER/DER) for byte-exact serialization (ITU page loaded live).

works.title: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)
works.authors: Anders Rundgren, Bret Jordan, Samuel Erdtman
works.note: The modern canonical-serialization treatment for JSON (deterministic form for hashing/signing), complementing DER's binary canon (RFC info page loaded live).

works.title: Nonstandard for Transmission of IP Datagrams over Serial Lines: SLIP
works.note: The classic END/ESC byte-stuffing framing spec - the minimal worked example every serial-framing design descends from (RFC info page loaded live).

works.title: Consistent Overhead Byte Stuffing
works.note: Naming paper for COBS - byte stuffing with tightly bounded worst-case overhead, now standard in embedded serial framing; IEEE/author pages not loadable this session.

works.title: Computer Networks (5th ed.)
works.authors: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, David J. Wetherall
works.note: The data-link framing chapter is the standard teaching treatment of bit stuffing, flag/byte stuffing, character-count (length) framing, and preambles/sync patterns; Tanenbaum's VU page (loaded) lists only the 4th ed., no 5th-ed identifier confirmed.

works.title: The Base16, Base32, and Base64 Data Encodings
works.note: The normative definition of the standard binary-to-text encodings (RFC info page loaded live).

works.title: HTTP/1.1
works.authors: R. Fielding, M. Nottingham, J. Reschke (eds.)
works.note: Current normative definition of chunked transfer coding - the canonical streaming length-delimited text framing (RFC info page loaded live).

works.title: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax
works.authors: T. Berners-Lee, R. Fielding, L. Masinter
works.note: Sec. 2.1 is the normative definition of percent-encoding (RFC info page loaded live).

works.title: Internet Protocol
works.note: Appendix B (data transmission order) is the primary definition of network byte order that htons/ntohl-style handling implements (RFC info page loaded live).

works.title: Delta Encoding in HTTP
works.authors: J. Mogul, B. Krishnamurthy, F. Douglis, A. Feldmann, Y. Goland, A. van Hoff, D. Hellerstein
works.note: Standards-grade naming and treatment of delta encoding (transmitting differences instead of full instances) (RFC info page loaded live).

works.title: Data Compression: The Complete Reference (4th ed.)
works.note: The comprehensive compression reference; its Basic Techniques chapter is the catalog-grade treatment of run-length encoding (Springer book page loaded live).

works.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
works.note: Ch. 4 'Encoding and Evolution' is the modern teaching treatment of tag-numbered fields and forward/backward-compatible schema evolution (official book site loaded live; ISBN via its O'Reilly link).

works.title: Effective Java (3rd ed.)
works.note: Item 90 names and teaches the serialization proxy pattern (InformIT publisher page loaded live). Distinct from corpus id 'bloch' (2006 API-design paper).

works.title: Serializer
works.authors: Dirk Riehle, Wolf Siberski, Dirk Baeumer, Daniel Megert, Heinz Zuellighoven
works.venue: Pattern Languages of Program Design 3, ch. 17, Addison-Wesley
works.note: The pattern-form definition of Serializer (stream objects to/from arbitrary backends); PLoPD3 TOC with the Serializer chapter loaded live on Riehle's site.

works.title: SAX (Simple API for XML) - official project documentation
works.note: The de-facto-standard event-based XML API whose docs ('Events vs. Trees') define push/event-driven parsing (official site loaded live).

works.title: Tolerant Reader (bliki)
works.note: Names and defines the Tolerant Reader pattern (Postel-style liberal parsing for evolvable integrations); notes Daigneau's Service Design Patterns as the full write-up (bliki loaded live, dated 9 May 2011).

works.title: file / libmagic (official project site and magic file documentation)
works.authors: Ian Darwin; maintained by Christos Zoulas et al.
works.note: The canonical operationalization of magic numbers / file signatures: the file command and libmagic identify formats by content signatures (official site loaded live).

works.title: ISO/IEC 9899 - Programming Languages - C
works.note: The C standard normatively defines escape sequences (\n, \xhh, ...), the definition every language's escape-sequence lexing inherits (WG14 official page loaded live confirming ISO/IEC 9899, C23 adopted 2024).

notes: All 41 r9 elements covered by >=1 catalog-grade work; no gaps. Parsing axis anchors: dragonbook + craftinginterpreters (7-8 elements each); serialization axis anchors: protobufenc (4 wire-format elements) + tanenbaumnet (4 framing elements). One membership: dwarf5 (LEB128 for varint). Six RFCs + X.690 + ISO C verified via rfc-editor/ITU/WG14 pages. Wikipedia-only named elements upgraded to catalog-grade sources: read-eval-print-loop -> craftinginterpreters, magic-number-file-signature -> file/libmagic official docs, sync-word -> tanenbaumnet framing chapter, run-length-encoding -> salomondc. 7 works unverified (ACM/IEEE DL and Pearson blocked fetches this session): knuth1965, pratt1973, thompson1968, oppen1980, parr2004, cobs1999 (all doi), tanenbaumnet (isbn) - each canon; identifiers omitted rather than guessed. Dragon Book year: route/catalog say 2006; Aho's verified page dates the Addison-Wesley printing 2007 - kept 2006 with note. Ford's PEG paper (POPL 2004) not added: no PEG element in this route; packrat-parsing carried by ford2002 alone.
